{"item":"i-0b6e","target":"t-35e20/i-0b6e","on":"2026-10-07","note":"Leases: a claim carries lease_until (default 30 min, [tickets] claim_lease_minutes, fractional allowed). Renewal sets the lock inode's mtime through the fd it read as the holder's (never rewrites a lock), so a renewal racing a reclaim extends only the claim it read. war heartbeat [<id>], and every war command (ambient actor) / ticket command (--as) / MCP and web ticket act renews. An expired lease: war ready offers it (expired_claim), a plain war claim reclaims it, journalled ticket.claim_reclaimed with from/from_since/from_lease_until. --steal kept for a live lease past the TTL (TTL counted from since, whatever the renewals). {"item":"i-5812","target":"t-35e20/i-5812","on":"2026-10-07","note":"Compare-and-set: --if-rev on done/edit/note/add/release (MCP if_rev on war_done/war_add/war_note; there are no MCP edit/release tools). Revisions are war model's (M3): ticket = sha256 of manifest bytes, item = sha256 of its checklist line; war show --json exposes revision and items[].revision. Stale -> warrant.stale-revision naming the current revision, nothing written. The plant's 4-way race found a base lost-update bug: atomic::write_if checks the prestate then renames (two steps), so two ticket rewrites could both pass and the second drop the first's line; ticket::rewrite now holds an flock on the file's directory across read-edit-rename."}

{"item":"i-5e12","target":"t-35e20/i-5e12","on":"2026-10-07","note":"[claims] remote = \"origin\" (off by default): a claim is also published as refs/openwarrant/claims/<lock name>, a --no-gpg-sign commit under a fixed war identity whose message is the claim, pushed with --atomic --force-with-lease (absent for a new claim), so the remote is the CAS arbiter. Local lock first, then the push; a lost push releases the local lock and is refused naming the remote holder. Expired remote leases are reclaimed (force-with-lease on the old commit), journalled with the remote ref. done verifies the remote still gives the claim, then deletes the ref with a lease; release deletes it if still ours. Remote leases renew on war heartbeat and on ticket commands past half-life. Unreachable remote: ticket.claim-remote-unreachable, nothing claimed. Plant: 2 clones x 4 agents race one item, exactly one wins. war serve NOT built (optional; deferred)."}

{"item":"i-75d0","target":"t-35e20/i-75d0","on":"2026-10-07","note":"Alias safety: war check refuses warrant.alias-duplicate when two Warrants answer to one alias (directory name or manifest local_alias), naming both dirs and UUIDs, with the renumber fix. war new allocates one past the highest ordinal in the working tree AND on every local and remote-tracking branch (one git for-each-ref + one git cat-file --batch reading raw trees; no per-branch process). war renumber <alias> <new> (new top-level command): unsigned only (authorization.toml or resolution.toml refused warrant.renumber-signed), new must parse in the namespace and be free in the tree, in any manifest's local_alias and on every branch (warrant.alias-taken); rewrites only the local_alias line, renames the directory, journals draft.renumbered."}
